sayLines.line: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 2). Falling pressure = weather coming. Your joints ache? That's a barometer. So are the birds — silent birds mean storm.
📖 LEARNED: Star Navigation (Level 2). The sun is a clock: east at dawn, south at noon (northern hemisphere), west at dusk. Shadows tell time.
📖 LEARNED: Cordage (Level 2). Reverse-wrap technique makes rope strong enough to hold weight. Braid for more strength.
📖 LEARNED: Reading the Water (Level 2). You read the day's water — temperature, clarity, current — and set your effort where the fish already are. Nets come up heavier.
📖 LEARNED: Swimmer (Level 1). Cross water freely. Rivers are roads to you.
📖 Your old life taught you things. 5 skills from your past — check your Journal.
This is home ground. You grew up on country like this.
📖 Your hands remember: knap a Stone knife (stone + vine) — the oldest tool there is. Find the stone.
📖 Your hands remember: weave cloth (3 plant fiber — strip it from cleared brush), and build a Water Filter (cloth + charcoal from fire ashes). Dirty water doesn't have to stay dirty.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Ryan Cooper. Sailor. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Trail compass, Dog tags, Photo album, Busker's harmonica, Knife roll. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. They found a deer this morn
A woman, maybe 30s, with weathered hands: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
You tell the others you're heading out. Someone nods. "Come back before dark."
